clauses.reason: The order restates Executive Order 8809 (as amended by 9323) as one paragraph establishing the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity, with eligibility by three years of service from August 27, 1940, one year of wartime service after December 7, 1941, or shorter honorable service after June 27, 1950, and a proviso against awards for under one year except for service-incurred disability. Executive Order 14085 section 2 (87 FR 60541; the order states no later effective date, so the signing date October 3, 2022 is used) amended that restated text: (a) striking "men" and inserting "members"; (b) inserting "and on or after December 20, 2019, in the case of the United States Space Force," after "August 27, 1940,"; (c) the same insertion after "December 7, 1941,"; and (d) inserting ", and on or after December 20, 2019, in the case of the United States Space Force" after "June 27, 1950". The amendment widens the persons and service covered and does not end the clause. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, the U.S. Code note still prints it as amended, and the order cites no authority statute that could lapse, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (18 FR 2069, signed 1953-04-10; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10444.txt). It further amends Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (Good Conduct Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9323 of March 31, 1943, to read as one restated paragraph, issued under the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces (no authority statute is cited). The restated text establishes the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity, under regulations the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force prescribe, for enlisted men of the Army and Air Force who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years of active Federal military service, or who after December 7, 1941 served one year of active Federal military service while the United States is at war, or who at termination of service had completed less than three years if any part was after June 27, 1950, with a proviso that no one, except persons separated by reason of physical disability incurred in line of duty, receives the medal for service of less than one year. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note that this order amends EO 8809 (with a see-reference to EO 9323); that is the order's own effect on its parent, not a later event against it. current-law:usc has 1 hit, the note at 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 that prints Ex. Ord. No. 8809 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 9323, Ex. Ord. No. 10444 (Apr. 10, 1953, 18 F.R. 2069) and Ex. Ord. No. 14085, sec. 2 (Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541), with no ending statement. current-law:ecfr has 0 hits. A search of the held texts for the number 10444 finds the order's own copies, Executive Order 14085, Executive Order 10445 (which makes conforming editorial notes in the Army and Air Force regulations in 32 CFR parts 578 and 878 and does not amend this order), the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification of EO 8809 (which records that EO 8809 was amended and restated by this order), and Federal Register pages of 1954 and 1967 whose authority citations name this order; none revokes or supersedes it. The one later amendment, Executive Order 14085 section 2 (87 FR 60541), is recorded as a later event with its before and after wording. The U.S. Code edition searched is release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it.

savings.reason: The order has no saving clause. It restates the parent order in full and issues no one-time command, so there is no pending-matter residue; the restated paragraph replaces the earlier text of Executive Order 8809 as amended by 9323. The bounded searches found no other residue or later instrument besides Executive Order 14085.
